entries.title: Deuteronomy 7:2
segments:
Thou shalt smite them, and utterly destroy them; the Israelites were the executioners of divine justice upon the Canaanites for their sins. 
 
In putting men to death according to God's directions, it is not needful or right to hate them, or have any unkind feelings towards them; and the idea that capital punishments spring from or imply any such feelings, is a great mistake.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 7:4
segments: Chosen and intimate connections with the openly wicked increase our danger of being drawn into sin, and should be carefully avoided.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 7:5
segments: Their groves; or, their images of Astarte.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 7:7
segments: Fewest of all; when God selected them and made promises to Abraham and his seed, they were very few; nor did they so greatly increase till near the time of their deliverance from Egypt.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 7:9
segments: The Lord will be faithful in fulfilling his promises to the righteous, and in executing his threatenings against the wicked.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 7:10
segments: Repay him to his face; promptly and openly punish him.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 7:14
segments: Obedience to God will procure the geatest blessings for this life and the life to come.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 7:19
segments: Temptations; trials; miracles by which God proved both Pharaoh and his own people.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 7:23
segments: Things which are done by God's direction, and which take place under his guiding and all-controlling providence, are in the Bible often spoken of as done by him.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 7:24
segments: The putting of criminals to death according to God's direction, is a proper expression of his just indignation against their sins; and when he commands, it cannot be neglected without disobeying him.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 7:25
segments: An abomination; having been used in idol-worship, the Israelites were to treat it with abhorrence, as a testimony against that sin.
